summary: Edition-2 book chapter III.3 (The Knowledge State and Its Eight Primitives): defines the time-indexed knowledge state K_t (K_{t+1}=Learn(K_t, Observations_t, Events_t, Policies_t, Outcomes_t)) over eight primitives {Entity, State, Event, Observation, Proposition, Relation, Policy, Action}, graded TESTED-within-scope on twelve reduction-falsification experiments plus a fifty-attack consistency audit; reproduces the source's reduction story from an initial four-core-plus-six-structure-family stratification down to the frozen eight-tuple; defines each primitive with notation/semantics/scope/grade/limitation; lists the derived-structure layer (Evidence=QualifiedObservation, Claim=Proposition, Identity=EntityIdentityRelation, Provenance=TypedDependencyRelation, Uncertainty=epistemic annotation U(C), Authority=governance structure, Decision=structure over K/S/Policy, Outcome=observed consequence, Learning/Revision/Drift=evolution structure); teaches PF-2 in place (the eight-primitive reduction argument is RECONSTRUCTABLE, but completeness/minimality/uniqueness remain explicitly NOT ESTABLISHED, per the source's own "candidate" framing); demonstrates the source's own failure case for collapsing typed relations into a generic RelatedTo edge (licensing an AI consumer to hallucinate causality); and walks a full election-certification K_t instance across all eight primitives.
contribution_assessment: A previously-unindexed book chapter supplying the full formal detail (notation, per-primitive definitions, the reduction derivation, the derived-structure equations) behind the eight-primitive kernel referenced elsewhere only as PF-2 in abbreviated form; teaches the exact boundary between what the reduction argument establishes (reconstructability) and what it explicitly does not (completeness/minimality/uniqueness), and supplies a concrete worked failure case for primitive mis-typing.

summary: Edition-2 book chapter III.8 (The Policy That Governs Itself), the full-depth expansion of the already-ratified policy-stratification content: teaches the policy-as-content/policy-in-force stratification and invariant I-11 verbatim; reproduces the PF-9 source governance algebra (context-indexed partial-order authority, applicability-precedes-conflict, three resolution instruments, three outcomes Resolved/Unresolved/Invalid); the escalation law (UnresolvedGovernanceConflict -> HumanGovernance, "knowing that something cannot be determined is itself a valid computed result"); the Instruction-vs-AuthorizedDecision distinction and the AI non-override clause at full source strength; and states the chapter's central answer -- four interlocking guards (mode separation, decision-under-contract, versioning with a transition schema, recursive self-subjection of the constitution to its own disciplines) that make self-modification governed rather than wild; closes with a mid-election policy-change running example and the constitutional-layer's independently-arrived-at parallel stratification (Chapter V).
contribution_assessment: Supplies the chapter-level synthesis binding the PF-9 governance algebra (already detailed in the production log, S1286) to invariant I-11 and to III.7's decision-contract machinery via a named four-guard structure explaining why the architecture's self-modification capability is governed rather than uncontrolled; states the AI non-override clause at full source strength and identifies it as the fourth of four independently-arrived-at statements of the same LLM-authority boundary across the book.

summary: Edition-2 book chapter III.5 (Evidence and Its Algebra), the full-depth expansion of evidence-algebra-invariants: defines Evidence as a qualified observation (Evidence=Observation+Relevance+Context; richer EXP-01 design tuple e=(P,pi,rho,kappa,tau,delta,...)); separates Existence from Sufficiency; states the three-layer evidence calculus (Representation/Aggregation/Inference, with Aggregation != Inference and both policy-indexed); reproduces the designed ten-criteria test suite (A-J) with each criterion's actual matrix-tested-or-not status (PF-4); describes the four candidate aggregation operators (max, weighted mean, saturating, Bayesian-like) and the executed matrix outcomes; reproduces the verdict's three-step reasoning for why no operator was selected despite two candidates passing all seven tested properties (the dependency argument establishing I-6, the duplicate/anti-amplification argument establishing I-5, and the preserved-structure argument); discloses and adjudicates the CSV-vs-prose-verdict discrepancy (GN-27 ruling: prose prevails, CSV graded unreliable-standalone) plus a GN-45 correction to the ratified grade-basis citation (AF-F-22); and gives negative and positive worked examples (a 41-item evidence flood collapsing to one real item; sufficiency achieved with only two items).
contribution_assessment: A major expansion supplying the exact formulas, the full ten-criteria table with per-criterion executed-vs-designed status, the four operators' pass/fail results, and the three-step verdict derivation (dependency, duplicate, preserved-structure arguments) behind the already-indexed I-5/I-6 invariants and the EXP-01 negative verdict -- previously only summarized in the object index -- plus new disclosure of a governance correction (GN-45, AF-F-22) to the ratified grade-basis citation.

summary: Edition-2 book chapter III.4 (Zero -- the Gap That Drives Inquiry): defines Zero(K,EC) as a directed, purpose-relative, structured epistemic discrepancy operator (never symmetric, never scoreless, never a number); teaches the source's nine-valued satisfaction status set (Satisfied/PartiallySatisfied/Unknown/Insufficient/Conflicted/Stale/Invalid/Prohibited/NotApplicable) and the Missing-vs-Unknown distinction (an absent required governed artifact vs a genuine evidentiary blank); shows PF-1's compression of the nine-status source into the ratified four-arm summary (unknown/conflicting/missing/invalid), disclosing that the "four-way" compression is embedded inside ratified invariant I-9's own wording (finding AF-F-9, corrected under GN-45); reproduces the source's own scalar-refusal argument (a count like "Zero=6" is meaningless when items are not comparable); separates Zero (gap detection) from the Proposal selector (gap-resolution planning, invariant I-2) and records PF-5(b), the source's unratified operational-vs-epistemic Zero split; and resolves a one-name-three-referents naming register (this chapter's L2 gap operator vs Z-KOS-001's meta-principle vs the historical absence-lens Zero) via chronology and a shared refusal rather than shared definition.
contribution_assessment: Supplies the full formal detail behind PF-1 and PF-5(b) (already summarized abstractly elsewhere in this batch), including the exact nine-status set, the Missing-vs-Unknown distinction, the operational-vs-epistemic Zero split, and a governance-relevant disclosure that the four-arm compression is not merely a summary artifact but appears inside a ratified invariant's own text (AF-F-9); also resolves a three-way naming collision on "Zero" via a fixed chronology, distinguishing this chapter's L2 gap operator from Z-KOS-001's meta-principle and the historical absence-lens sense.
